proposed_meta_description: Professional AC service: inspection, flush, vacuum & recharge at South Hill Goodyear. R-134A from $116.99. Call (253) 840-0995.
proposed_h1: Professional AC Recharge Service at South Hill Goodyear
proposed_highlights: Complete AC service in one appointment: inspection, system flush, vacuum, and refrigerant recharge
Two refrigerant options available: R-134A for $116.99 or R-1234yf for $215.99 — up to 1 lb refrigerant included
Professional Goodyear-certified technicians at a trusted national brand location
System leak check included — if a leak is detected during inspection, technician will diagnose and explain repair options
[Example — verify with merchant:] Typical service time 45–90 minutes; plan accordingly or ask about wait/drop-off options
Appointment required for all services — call (253) 840-0995 to schedule at a time that works for you
Perfect for seasonal maintenance — may be repurchased every 30 days to keep your AC running at peak performance
pricing_framing: Drop the unverifiable 'Up To 53% OFF' claim (no original price exists to support it; value_comm: 4/10). Instead, frame against the validated market range of $122–$179 (RepairPal estimate for AC service in South Hill). Position as: 'Groupon price $116.99 (R-134A) — $5 below the typical $122+ market rate' or 'Save vs. the $122–$179 market range for AC recharge services.' This honest positioning is more credible than an unsupported discount percentage and still communicates clear value.
executive_summary: The page scores 5.5/10 overall, dragged down by a critical value communication failure: it claims 'Up To 53% OFF' but shows no original price, leaving customers unable to verify the deal (value_comm: 4/10). The actual deal is solid — $116.99 vs. a $122–$179 market range — but the page doesn't communicate it. Three fixes would lift conversion 20–30%: (1) Replace the unverifiable '53% OFF' claim with '$5 below typical $122+ market price', (2) remove the live 'Insert custom text' placeholder destroying trust, and (3) rewrite the highlights to explain what customers actually get instead of just listing refrigerant types.
